S53.01.note: The Skills screen is also reachable from search under Go to > Skills (apps/mobile/src/features/search/mobileDestinations.ts).
steps: Sign in and switch to AGI Cloud (the Cloud chat mode).
Open the side menu, tap Settings, then tap Customize in the Cloud group.
Tap Skills in the Customize list. The Skills screen opens with a Search skills field.
Scroll the list. Skills that are not installed show the status Not installed and an Install button, so the catalogue includes them.
Compare with Expected: you can browse skills not yet installed and tap Details on any of them.

S53.02.note: The earlier DrawerContent.tsx:115 reference no longer exists and the drawer shows no skills list; the installed list lives only on the Skills screen.
steps: Sign in and switch to AGI Cloud.
Open the side menu, tap Settings, tap Customize, then tap Skills.
Read the line at the top of the list: it shows a count such as 1 SKILL INSTALLED or N SKILLS INSTALLED.
Look at the status line on each card: Installed or Not installed.
Compare with Expected: the list shows which skills are installed for the account.

S53.03.needs: A Cloud account that the server allows to author skills (if the buttons are missing the account is not allowed)
S53.03.note: Whether a given account is allowed to author skills is decided by the server flag canAuthorSkills (apps/mobile/src/features/skills/service.ts), so the tester may not see these buttons; the plan's note that New skill is built is consistent with the code.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud and open Settings > Customize > Skills.
Look for the New skill and Import buttons above the list. They appear only when the server says this account can author skills.
Tap New skill, fill in the Skill name, Skill description and Skill instructions fields, then tap Create skill.
Find the new skill in the list and check its source tag reads Personal.
Tap Details on it and check the Make your own section shows Edit instructions and Delete skill.
Open Settings > Customize > Skills.
Read the bold name on each card, and the grey line under it.
Find a skill with no description and check it shows No description provided.
Tap Details on any card and check the name shows at the top of the skill screen.
Compare with Expected: each skill shows its name and a description of what it does.

labels.text: Install a Skill to use it in your AGI Cloud messages.

S53.08.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account with Cloud mode on; at least one installed skill to see the Use in chat button
S53.08.note: The Turned-on skills line is in apps/mobile/src/features/skills/SkillDetailScreen.tsx and the @ trigger is in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/fileMention.ts; the Skills row in the + sheet appears only in Cloud mode.
steps: Open Settings > Customize > Skills and read the line under the Skills heading: Install a Skill to use it in your AGI Cloud messages.
Tap Details on an installed skill and read the line Turned-on skills load in your Cloud chats when a task needs them.
Open a Cloud chat and tap the + button (Add to chat); look for a Skills row showing Choose or the selected skill name.
In the chat box type @ and look for the Skills to use list.
Compare with Expected: the product states how a skill is used (a button, an @ mention, or automatic matching).
S53.08.where: Settings > Customize > Skills, then the + button (Add to chat) in a Cloud chat

S53.14.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account and a skill that declares required tools
S53.14.note: The card text is built in apps/mobile/src/features/skills/SkillsScreen.tsx (skillRequirementNote); enforcement when a turn is sent is in apps/mobile/src/features/skills/skillRequirements.ts and is not visible on screen.
steps: Open Settings > Customize > Skills.
Find a card that has a line starting Needs followed by tool names.
Tap Details on that card.
Find the Needs section and check it lists Tools: followed by the same tool names.
Compare with Expected: the skill declares the tools it needs and the product shows them.
S53.14.where: Settings > Customize > Skills (card line Needs ...), then Details (section Needs)

S53.17.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one installed skill, and Cloud mode
S53.17.note: Whether the model actually used the skill is visible only in the reply content, not as a UI marker; the code only sends the skill name with the turn (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx).
steps: Open Settings > Customize > Skills and tap Use in chat on an installed skill.
Back in the chat, look for a chip with the skill name above the text box, with an x button labelled Clear selected Skill.
Type a message and send it in Cloud mode.
Read the reply and check whether it follows the chosen skill's instructions.
Compare with Expected: the picked skill is used for that message. The chip disappears after sending.
S53.17.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > Use in chat (installed skill), then the chat box

S53.18.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account with an installed skill
S53.18.note: No visible indicator of automatic matching was found in the mobile code; the mobile surface is not excluded from the offer (only vscode, cli and api are excluded).
steps: Install a skill that has a clear description, such as a skill about writing emails.
Open a Cloud chat without picking a skill and send a message that matches that description.
Read the reply and check whether it follows the skill's instructions.
Compare with Expected: the skill is used without being asked. No visible marker in the mobile app was found to confirm it.
S53.18.where: Server side: when a Cloud message has no skill picked, the server offers installed skills whose descriptions match the message (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts)
